testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Close your eyes as vehicles approach.
Look at the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: When oncoming headlights blind you, glance to the right side of the road. Keep looking there until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: When changing lanes, but only if other vehicles are nearby.
When changing lanes, but only if it is dark outside.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors before changing lanes. Check them frequently as part of your normal driving routine.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Do this even during the day.

questions.question: What is the purpose of header boards?

options.text: They protect the driver from cargo moving forward.
They protect the driver's head when getting into the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: They protect the driver from cargo moving forward.
questions.explanation: Header boards, called "headache racks," protect the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel.
With both hands at the top of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel with both hands. Place them on opposite sides of the wheel and grip it firmly.

questions.question: What should you know about joggers wearing headsets?

options.text: They are usually aware of what is happening around them.
They may not be aware of what is happening around them.
They can clearly hear traffic sounds.
They usually don't have music playing.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic and may not know you are there.

questions.question: What should you do when construction workers are near the road?

options.text: Do not drive in any lane.

questions.explanation: In construction zones, do not exceed the posted speed limit. Slow down even more when workers are near the road.

questions.question: What is a good rule to follow when making a turn?

options.text: Use your arms to get other drivers' attention.
Turn off your turn signal before the turn to avoid confusing other drivers.

questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know your plans. Keep the signal on during the turn. Turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: What should you do when asked to change lanes during a driving test?

options.text: Change lanes right away without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as quickly as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When the test examiner asks you to change lanes, check traffic first. Use your turn signal before changing lanes safely.

questions.question: What should you do if you are unsure your vehicle will fit under a bridge?

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, slow down. Find another route if possible.

questions.question: If a driver feels tired while driving, what should they do?
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy while driving, you must safely pull off the road and sleep. Coffee and other stimulants are dangerous because they can cause extreme tiredness when they wear off.

questions.question: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, what should a driver do?

options.text: Go forward straight, then back to the left.
Go back straight, then forward to the left.
Go forward straight, then back straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go forward straight, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first go straight forward, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must fit completely within the parking space.

questions.question: When are most drivers the least alert?
questions.explanation: Tiredness and lack of alertness are major dangers when driving at night. Most people are least alert at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks?
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks during a driving test, you must not stop, change gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: For exercises other than straight line backing, how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during skills tests. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you can look one time. For other exercises, you can look two times.

questions.question: What should you do when backing with a trailer?

options.text: You should not back up in a straight line.
You should not fix drift until you are far off course.
You should move forward often to reposition the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should move forward often to reposition the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When backing, move forward to reposition your vehicle whenever needed. Fix drift right away by turning the steering wheel toward the drift direction.

questions.question: When starting the vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, what should the coolant temperature do?
questions.explanation: After starting your vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, watch the gauges. The coolant temperature should gradually rise to normal operating range.

questions.question: What color lights show that anti-lock brakes are not working?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with anti-lock braking systems have yellow lights that turn on when there is a problem with the brakes.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver confronts you, stay safe by getting out of their way. Do not make eye contact, do not speed up to challenge them, and do not react to their angry gestures.

questions.question: What does a high center of gravity do?

options.text: Makes a vehicle more likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes a vehicle more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need each night to stay alert?
questions.explanation: Getting enough rest is critical for safe driving. Most people need eight to nine hours of sleep each night to stay alert.

questions.question: What is another name for front-end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are also called "headache racks." They protect the driver if cargo shifts forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: When checking springs during a vehicle inspection, do all of the following except:

options.text: Check that torsion springs are not damaged.

questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs. Also look for broken or bent coil springs. If the vehicle has torsion bars or other suspension parts, make sure they are not damaged and are securely mounted. Do not glue cracked springs.

questions.question: When entering a foggy area, you should:

options.text: Stop on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Slow down before entering fog. Use low beam headlights. Do not pass other vehicles or stop on the roadway. The safest choice is to avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.question: Transporting hanging meat in a trailer:

options.text: Can be problematic because animals are attracted to the smell.
Is challenging because the load has a high center of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is challenging because the load has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat loads are unstable. They have a high center of gravity, and the swinging meat can affect how you control the vehicle. You must drive with extra care.

questions.question: When completing an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, first pull straight forward. Then back up to the right. Park your vehicle completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection:

options.text: Should never be completed the same way twice.
Should always be completed in the same order.
Should only be done when it is sunny.
Should not be done if the vehicle seems to be working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always be completed in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This habit helps you remember all the steps and prevents you from forgetting to check something important.

questions.question: Cargo should be checked:

options.text: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.
Only by the people who loaded it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, again within the first 50 miles, then every three hours or every 150 miles. Also check it whenever you stop for a break. You are responsible for keeping cargo secure during the entire trip.

questions.question: Aggressive driving is:

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy manner.
Driving with concern for other motorists' safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy manner.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy way without concern for others' rights or safety.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a cause for concern since it is stopped.
Is only a concern if passengers are getting out.
Is always a concern, whether or not you see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a concern, whether or not you see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be cautious near a stopped bus. Passengers may be nearby. The bus can block your view or hide passengers from seeing you.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back right parking, offset back left parking, driver side parallel parking, standard parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: A steering wheel should be:

options.text: Held with one hand while the other rests.
Held with both hands for a firm grip.
Released if the vehicle hits a bump.

questions.correctAnswerText: Held with both hands for a firm grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: An after-trip inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Complete an after-trip inspection of your vehicle at the end of every trip, day, or work period. Fill out a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: You should check and adjust your mirrors:
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Your position may change each day, so mirrors may need adjustment.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, the rods move the slack adjusters when air pressure enters the brake chambers. The driver adds this air pressure by:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out the rods and moves slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, and other vehicles with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1998, must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: Drivers are usually the least alert:
questions.explanation: Drivers are usually less alert when driving at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: A fatigued driver:

options.text: Should take over-the-counter medicine to stay awake.
May make important decisions too slowly.
Is usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make important decisions too slowly.
questions.explanation: When fatigued, you will not see or react to hazards as quickly as when you are rested. You will have trouble making important decisions.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, your minimum following distance should be:
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection portion of the skills test, an applicant must:

options.text: Explain to the examiner what to check and why.
Let the examiner check the vehicle.
Talk to a mechanic to show knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what to check and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection skills test, you must explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may mean the driver is:

options.text: Using the heat in their vehicle.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. A driver who has drunk too much, is tired, is using drugs, or is sick can be dangerous. An open window in cold weather may be a sign the driver is impaired.

questions.question: If you feel sleepy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving to finish your trip.
Drive faster to get there sooner.
Pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel sleepy while driving, the only safe thing to do is stop and sleep. Fighting tiredness is dangerous and causes many fatal crashes. Energy pills are not safe because they wear off and then you will be even more tired.

questions.question: When driving a commercial motor vehicle:

options.text: You do not have to wear a safety belt.
You only have to wear a safety belt if your vehicle has no airbags.
You only have to wear a safety belt if you are carrying more than 1,000 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a safety belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a safety belt.
questions.explanation: A safety belt is your best protection in a crash. You must always wear a safety belt when driving a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: To do an offset back/left parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Go straight forward, then back to the right.
Go straight forward, then back to the left.
Go forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Go forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, go straight forward first. Then back up to the left. Your vehicle must be completely inside the parking space lines.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a header board, it should:

options.text: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: When you check the header board during a vehicle inspection, make sure it is secure, has no damage, and is strong enough to hold cargo.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Get enough sleep before you drive
Schedule trips during hours when you would normally be asleep

questions.correctAnswerText: Schedule trips during hours when you would normally be asleep
questions.explanation: Tired driving is very dangerous. To prevent drowsiness, get a full night's sleep before your trip, have someone drive with you, schedule trips when you are normally awake, and avoid medicines that cause drowsiness.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Grip between the tires and the road
How long it takes for the brakes to work

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip between the tires and the road
questions.explanation: Traction is the grip between your tires and the road. Good traction is needed to stop and steer safely.

questions.question: What comes out when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil that builds up. If water and oil stay in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If a speed limit is posted, the posted speed:

options.text: Can be exceeded when passing another vehicle.
Can be exceeded in rural areas.

questions.explanation: A posted speed limit is the fastest you can go under perfect conditions. You must slow down when conditions require it. You should never go faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: If you do not drain air tanks, you could have:

options.text: Water freezing and causing brake failure.
Too much air in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water freezing and causing brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.
